speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: asked	the Minister for Transport what are the reasons for LTA or SMRT not releasing public information on the discovery of hairline cracks on the MRT trains in July 2013 and on their subsequent decision to call on the warranty by shipping the affected trains back to the manufacturer's factory for defect rectification works.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: asked	the Minister for Transport whether Kawasaki Heavy Industries and CSR Sifang are liable to compensate LTA and/or SMRT for any loss of use and/or profits (or any other damages suffered) for the downtime of the MRT trains sent back to the manufacturer's factory for rectification in addition to the shipping and defect rectification costs.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether the hairline cracks found on the car-body bolster of the affected MRT trains were inherent defects from the time LTA and/or SMRT accepted delivery of the trains in 2011 or defects that were manifested through use and subsequently discovered in July 2013; (b) if the hairline cracks were inherent defects, why were the defects not discovered through earlier routine checks; and (c) if these were defects manifested through use, whether LTA engineers expect the hairline cracks to worsen through continued use.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Question Nos 8, 9, 10 are possible, Minister.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Question No 12 is not possible because you are skipping Question No 11.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Then, I shall come to it when the turn comes up.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not uncommon for new trains to develop minor defects after some time, because they are subject to different levels of stress during testing and when they are deployed for actual operations.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: LTA did not publicise the hairline cracks for three reasons.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, they did not pose any safety risk to commuters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, I wanted to reply to Question No 12 so that I can elaborate on this point, but we shall come to it later.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Third, the manufacturer accepted LTA's replacement work schedule which is deliberately formulated to ensure that train services and capacity levels are not affected by this incident.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Had any of these factors not been satisfactorily dealt with, LTA would have publicised the defects.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Meanwhile, we continue to monitor the affected trains closely, including those which had 	Page: 19 been rectified by the manufacturer.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Can the Minister provide more information to the House, please?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We handled the defective bolsters in such a way that we make sure that the planned capacity expansion of the North-South East-West line will not be affected.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Had the manufacturer wanted LTA to return all the 26 trains in one go, then our plan to expand the capacity of the North-South East-West lines would have been affected.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why, in 2013, LTA worked out a schedule to which the manufacturer accepted that they will only take one train at a time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In that way, the capacity will not be affected too much because all operators of train service would allow for at least a 10% buffer.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For example, for North-South East-West lines, although we have 140-plus trains, only 124 are fully launched at peak hours.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: All the new trains will continue to come.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But because we would only release one train at a time for the manufacturer to fix the bolsters, it does not affect our buffer and, therefore, it does not affect our planned capacity expansion of the North-South East-West lines.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To reiterate the point, this is also the reason why the whole process of rectifying, seemingly, takes such a long time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Actually, to fix the bolsters only requires about three to four months.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The manufacturer has to dismantle the trains, remove the bolsters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The bolsters are actually welded to the car body.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, they have to be sent over to China and then to be welded to brand new car bodies and the manufacturer has to re-assemble all the engines and so on, to the train.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The whole process would take about four months, including testing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Having completed this whole re-assembly, you have to test the trains to make sure they are safe and functioning as required.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But because each time we can only release one train, so we have to queue up the trains and we have a work schedule that stretches all the way to beyond 2020.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Recently, we sat down with the manufacturer and asked to speed this up a bit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This has nothing to do with the new Kawasaki trains, but yes, it happened yesterday.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is the first-generation Kawasaki train; not this current generation, which is having the bolsters problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The train and air-con compressors are all 20-odd years old by now.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Preliminary investigation suggests that there was a leakage of the oil from the compressor which resulted in overheating of the compressor.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Subsequently, that caused the evaporation of the freon, which was then released.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This morning, the engineers are going to pull apart the whole compressor to see what caused the leakage from the compressor shaft seal.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There is a seal which keeps the oil in place.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There is a three-weekly check on the compressor as part and parcel of routine maintenance and the last time we checked on this particular compressor was only about 10 days ago, in the early part of August.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, we need to know what is the reason for this incident.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There is a lesson here, even though it was about train.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Old assets are not the same as new assets and, therefore, you have to pay particular attention to maintenance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But the earlier part of the life history of the components is also important.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If you look after your body well from Day 1, when you are 40-50 years old, you can probably still maintain pretty good form, but still a 40-year-old is not the same as a 14-year-old, and, likewise, it is the same with trains.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I ask this because there was one reported case, I believe, of the explosion of a battery, affecting this batch, the C151A batch.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And then there were also a number of cases which affected, I think, five trains of shattering glass screens.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Have there been any other inherent manufacturing defects that have been discovered?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And what is the role of Kawasaki Heavy Industries in this?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, when the trains return, will there be a warranty period for them?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When they tendered for this, it was Kawasaki with the Chinese company Sifang.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think they are from Qingdao in the Shandong area.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But the main contractor, as far as we are concerned, is Kawasaki.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, the bulk of the design, how it is laid out, the engines and so on, were all from Kawasaki.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, they produce the bolsters which are made in China; secondly, they produce the car bodies; and thirdly, they assemble.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, all the engines or whatever parts that go into a train – if they are not produced in China, and most of them are not – they will be sent to Qingdao and then Sifang Company will do the assembly, do the testing, and then they will export it to whoever is the customer, in this case, Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As far as we are concerned, the party that we interact with is Kawasaki.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, Kawasaki set up an office here in Singapore for many years now because they were also the manufacturer, designer and producer of our first set of Kawasaki trains; in fact, of our first set of Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The first lines, North-South East-West lines, were all based on Kawasaki trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is a very established, good company that has been around for many, many years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Their arrangement to do the various assembly work in China is not unique to Kawasaki.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, in recent tenders, when we look at the bids, whether it is from Siemens, Bombardier, almost all of 	Page: 21 them now partner China to do the various things, very similar to what Kawasaki is doing with Sifang, I suppose, partly because of cost competitiveness, in order to bring down the cost of their total bids.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The way Kawasaki dealt with this whole incident – I have not met them but based on reports and discussions I have had with LTA as well as SMRT – I have been very impressed with the way they dealt with this problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There will always be problems, but at the end of the day, when confronted with a problem, how do you handle it?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There are people who will deny, blame others, but in this case, Kawasaki took immediate attention, sent their engineers down, checked, identified the primary cause and, at the same time, worked out how to move from there.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is a very professional response to this problem which I find very impressive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They took responsibility and fulfilled the warranty period commitments.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They require the Chinese partner to also produce the new aluminium car bodies, weld it, assemble it and retest it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I find that gesture on the part of Kawasaki highly commendable and, if I may say, generous.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The point about other defects of this train, such as battery.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As we know, when train cars are manufactured or assembled, a lot of testing will be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: During one of those tests, they found that one of the batteries was defective where gases were somehow accumulated in the housing that holds the battery covers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because of the accumulation of gas, it exploded.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They also redesign the housing, so that this problem will not repeat.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Indeed, it was the only incident of this kind which happened.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There were a few cases of glass shattering, not the main glass for the car but on those side windows.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They checked and they found that there was installation error.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In other words, the workers could have done it better.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Subsequently, when they reminded the workers to do the installation properly, we never heard of such incidents again.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Also, when we get the replacement car body and bolster, when we reset the clock, is it just resetting the clock on the car body and bolster?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The whole machinery and engine are also disassembled and assembled on the new car body.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does the reset of the warranty also apply to the mechanical parts?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is fair that the extended warranty only applies to the new bolster and the car bodies.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It will be asking too much to require the extended warranty to also cover the engines and other parts, which may not be produced by them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, sometimes, in public communications, providing more information is better than less information.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: My colleagues who have worked with me now for almost 40 years, know that I always prescribe the principle of over-provide rather than under-provide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is something that I learnt, especially during the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) period, in crisis communications.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because at that time, there was a lot of misinformation, a lot of lack of information, a lot of lies going on.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And always coming out to share with the people what you know, including what you do not know and admit that "Yes, I do not know at this point in time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And when I find out, I will let people know.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is always a better strategy than to try to keep information to your chest.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The second lesson will be, I was struck by how the Kawasaki Manufacturer reacted to this problem: face the problem, get to the bottom of it, own it, not in denial and then go all out to do what is right, even if it means at great cost to the company.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That way, you preserve integrity, reputation and also, that is the way one should treat one's customers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There is still a series of Parliamentary Questions (PQs) to be answered later.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The other questions are also related to trains.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The other one I will reserve for the next set of questions.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: For those trains that are awaiting to be sent back to China and they are in service now, are there any cracks found on the body because the cracks originated from the car body bolster?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Are there any cracks found on the body now or developing?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: No, the cracks are only on the bolsters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is North-South East-West lines, so each train has six cars.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This only happens in some bolsters of some train cars.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Have we ever experienced similar hairline cracks on other trains or models and, if so, what are the models?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These are Bombardier LRT trains, different from MRT trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They found some cracks on the underframe of the cars.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This was about last year or the year before.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They should be 	Page: 23 coming to 20 years, 18 years or so.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The nature of the cracks is quite different because here, with the Sifang trains, the trains are brand new.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I sent to you and then after operation, we found some cracks.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Whereas Bombardier trains, they were all right until last year or so, and then there were some cracks on the underframe.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Bombardier also took it quite seriously even though this is now an 18-year-old or 17-year-old product.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They sent their chief structural engineer down to take a look, inspect.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, they needed to establish if it was safe to operate, and they confirmed that it was safe to operate.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Then, they also decided on what the next step should be.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The next step requires regular inspection to see whether it is growing but, more importantly, how to fix the problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In that instance, the recommendation of the Bombardier chief structural engineer is to weld it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Therefore, there is no need to send it anywhere.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, they can weld it, in situ, locally in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They worked out a work schedule on how to do it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think most of the trains have already been fixed.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The other train cars should all be completed by October this year, if I am not mistaken.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Meanwhile, the trains are safe to be used.
